newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse ends down in scandal sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse ends down in scandal sell-off.

text.p: The Athens bourse closed 3.31 percent down after a day of steady selling in low to moderate turnover.
It was the first normal session since a settlement scandal halted trading for almost four days, and brokers and analysts predicted that the fall would continue for a few days.
"Market sentiment is not good right now. Retail as well as institutional investors were selling today obviously affected by the bourse's closure," said a floor trader who requested anonymity.
"Fundamentally, nothing has changed. Today's sell-off had a big psychological component and it might take some time before the wounds are healed," he said.
"Optimism is a scarce commodity in times such as these but this episode could well turn out to be a blessing in disguise in the medium turn leading to a stronger, healthier market," the broker said.

ING Barings said in its daily commentary that the bourse authorities would have to come up with a plan to avoid similar crises in the future and the government appeared more determined to get tougher with brokers who fail to settle on time.
"However, the mechanism for detecting brokers who are selling with continuous rollovers will continue to be weak until book-entry settlement is introduced in early 1997," it said.

The 65-member Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEXA), angered by perceived inaction by the authorities to probe the Delta scandal, refused to trade on Friday and effectively closed the bourse for four days.
Bourse authorities on Thursday ordered a two-day suspension in trade in four stocks linked to the Delta settlement scandal.
Magrizos, Parnassos, Hellenic Sugar Industry and St George Mills were suspended from trading on Thursday and Friday, a bourse statement said.
"The suspension is not related to the companies or their financial situation but will facilitate any possible checks being conducted on transactions in their shares to date," the statement said.
The national economy ministry has ordered an audit of 10 brokerages.

The order came after one brokerage, Delta Securities, tried to settle at the bourse clearing house with bad checks. That led to an uproar by the brokers' association which demanded that the government guarantee future settlements.
The Athens bourse closed 3.31 percent or 30.04 points lower at 878.38 points after opening at 908.07. Turnover was moderate at 5.019 billion drachmas.

Losers led gainers 175 to 18 with 14 issues unchanged on 207 traded. Banks lost 3.71 percent, industrials closed 3.66 percent lower with construction plunging 6.70 percent. Small-caps climbed 3.79 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE Telecom with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas closed at 535-553. Shares of OTE ended unchanged at 4,075 drachmas.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $7.06-$8.06. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 2,300-2,448 drachmas at the close.
